content.text:
At the café, the barista asks, “For here?” Your answer: 포장해 주세요. (“To go, please.”) Say it now; in 3 minutes, try again without the cards.

For another café turn, Language Cafe’s free Korean café mission lets you order a drink and answer the next question. Log in to start; no card required.

Try it → https://languagestudio.uk/missions/korean-cafe/?utm_source=threads&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=language_cafe&utm_content=takeaway-3card-20260926

images.altText: At a Korean café, a mint mascot points to a takeaway bag. 포장해 주세요. means To go, please.
In a café dialogue, staff asks 매장에서 드시나요? and the customer answers 포장해 주세요.
A three-minute recall exercise asks you to say the takeaway line again, then points to a separate free Korean café mission linked in the caption.

koreanExpressionAccuracy.evidence: 포장해 주세요. is a natural polite café response to 매장에서 드시나요? when the order is to go.

englishExplanation.evidence: To go, please. is a concise natural meaning for the polite Korean takeaway request in this exchange.

mobileLegibility.evidence: All three 1080x1350 cards and the 270-pixel phone preview were visually checked; target Hangul, English dialogue, recall cue and mission invitation are readable without clipping.

siteOfferAccuracy.evidence: Fresh public GETs confirmed the homepage links to the free Korean café pilot. The mission asks for login, needs no card, and covers a café order and next question; the post does not promise this exact expression in the mission.

draftEvidence.note: The separate editorial grant must match this final job and its hosted assets before scheduling. This new job does not retry the abandoned first action.
